summary: Shader-driven screen transition (radial wipe, dissolve) instead of a flat colour fade.
overview: The fancier alternative to a colour fade: any material whose shader exposes a _Progress float can drive the transition. Kept as a separate component rather than folded into FadeManager, so the plain fade stays simple and needs no material.
useCases: A radial wipe or iris between scenes.
A dissolve or burn transition matching a game's art direction.
Any custom transition, by writing a shader with one progress property.

params.tuning: The shader MUST expose a float named _Progress, and must declare a _MainTex texture property even if it never samples it (see gotchas). A material without _Progress fails silently — nothing animates and nothing logs.

gotchas.title: The material is shared state
gotchas.body: Driving the same material asset from two transitions at once fights. Instance it if that is possible in your setup.

gotchas.title: A custom transition shader must declare _MainTex, even unused
gotchas.body: The overlay is a UI Image, and a UI Graphic binds its own texture into _MainTex on every mesh rebuild. A shader without the property makes Unity log "doesn't have a texture property '_MainTex'" over and over — which is what all seven Toolkit/ScreenTransitions shaders used to do. They now declare it as an unused white texture. Do the same in your own: the effect never has to sample it, the binding just needs somewhere to land.
